name: Procaterol

overview.mechanism: Beta2-adrenergic stimulation produces bronchodilation; clinical applicability depends on the respiratory diagnosis and formulation [[PROC-ASTHMA]].
uses: Oral procaterol has been studied in reversible airway disease. This historical trial does not define a contemporary asthma treatment pathway or inhaled-product indication [[PROC-ASTHMA]].

evidence.title: Clinical evidence and limitations
evidence.intro: Study regimens are descriptions of research, not prescribing recommendations.

rows.design: Double-blind placebo comparison; 45 adults; two weeks.
rows.intervention: Two oral procaterol regimens versus placebo in chronic reversible airway disease.
rows.findings: Spirometry improved versus placebo. Tremor and nervousness were dose-related, mild/transient and most apparent early in treatment.
rows.limitations: Small, short historical oral-drug trial; no evidence here of mortality benefit, exacerbation prevention or severe-CKD safety.

rows.design: Randomized double-blind placebo trial; 74 nonasthmatic adults; four weeks.
rows.intervention: Oral procaterol versus placebo for cough persisting ≥3 weeks after respiratory infection.
rows.findings: No significant benefit in cough-specific quality of life, spirometry or impulse oscillometry. Both groups improved over time.
rows.limitations: Results distinguish postinfectious cough from asthma; bronchodilator efficacy in reversible obstruction should not be generalized to all persistent cough.

sources.citation: A placebo-controlled trial of procaterol: a new long-acting oral beta 2-agonist in bronchial asthma. PubMed PMID: 2861219.
Effects of Oral Procaterol for Postinfectious Cough in Adults: Single-Centre, Randomized Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial. PubMed PMID: 32403902.

common: Tremor and nervousness were the most frequent adverse effects in the short oral-asthma trial; its lack of significant ECG or laboratory changes does not exclude uncommon toxicity [[PROC-ASTHMA]].

renal: The cited studies do not establish a CKD adjustment or dialysis schedule. No renal dose is inferred from healthy-subject pharmacology or beta-agonist class practice [[PROC-ASTHMA,PROC-COUGH]].
